title: Entropy bounds for slowly rotating black holes in de Sitter space
abstract: We derive upper bounds on the horizon entropy of slowly rotating black holes embedded in de Sitter space. The bounds follow from a first law that includes the cosmological horizon, and they tighten the Bekenstein estimate for small rotation.

title: Hawking radiation spectra from charged dilaton black holes
abstract: Using a semiclassical tunnelling method we compute the emission spectrum of charged dilaton black holes. Greybody factors are obtained numerically, and the dilaton coupling suppresses the emission of charged particles near extremality.

title: A heat-engine view of AdS black hole thermodynamics
abstract: Treating the cosmological constant as pressure, we construct heat engines whose working substance is an anti-de Sitter black hole. We compare their efficiency with the Carnot bound and identify cycles that approach it in the large-charge limit.

title: Phase transitions of black holes with nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: We study the extended phase space of black holes sourced by Born-Infeld electrodynamics. The equation of state shows a small-large black hole transition with critical exponents that match mean-field theory.

title: Quantum corrections to the Bekenstein-Hawking area law
abstract: Logarithmic corrections to black hole entropy are computed from the one-loop effective action of matter fields on the horizon. The coefficient depends on the field content and constrains models of quantum gravity.

title: Information recovery from evaporating black holes via island formulas
abstract: We apply the island prescription for entanglement entropy to an evaporating two-dimensional black hole coupled to a bath. The resulting Page curve rises and falls, consistent with unitary evaporation.

title: Thermodynamic geometry of rotating black strings
abstract: We compute the Ruppeiner curvature of rotating black strings and relate its sign to the nature of microscopic interactions. Divergences of the curvature coincide with the onset of thermodynamic instability.

title: Black hole chemistry in higher-curvature gravity
abstract: Gauss-Bonnet corrections change the critical behaviour of charged black holes in five dimensions. We map the phase diagram and find reentrant phase transitions for a range of couplings.

title: Evaporation of primordial black holes in an expanding universe
abstract: We follow the mass loss of primordial black holes through radiation and matter domination. Accretion from the cosmic background delays evaporation for masses above a threshold that we compute.

title: Surface gravity and temperature of dynamical horizons
abstract: We propose a definition of surface gravity for slowly evolving dynamical horizons and show that it reproduces the Hawking temperature in the stationary limit.

title: Entanglement witnesses for multipartite photonic states
abstract: We construct entanglement witnesses tailored to six-photon graph states. The witnesses need only two local measurement settings, which makes them practical for current photonic experiments.

title: Quantum error correction with biased-noise qubits
abstract: When dephasing dominates bit-flip errors, tailored surface codes reach higher thresholds. We simulate codes adapted to biased noise and report thresholds above five percent for strong bias.

title: Mutual information and entanglement in free fermion chains
abstract: We compute the mutual information between disjoint blocks of a free fermion chain. Its scaling with separation distinguishes critical from gapped phases and agrees with conformal field theory predictions.

title: Variational quantum eigensolvers for small molecules on noisy hardware
abstract: We benchmark a hardware-efficient variational eigensolver on lithium hydride and water. Error mitigation by zero-noise extrapolation recovers chemical accuracy for the smaller molecule.

title: Quantum channel capacities with entanglement assistance
abstract: We give closed-form entanglement-assisted capacities for a family of non-Pauli qubit channels and show that shared entanglement can double the classical capacity at high noise.

title: Learning quantum states with classical shadows
abstract: Randomized measurements yield classical shadows from which many properties of a quantum state can be predicted. We study the sample complexity of entanglement entropy estimates and test the method on simulated data.

title: Teleportation fidelity under correlated noise
abstract: Correlated dephasing between sender and receiver lowers teleportation fidelity less than independent noise of the same strength. We derive the fidelity for Gaussian-correlated channels.

title: Scrambling and operator growth in random circuits
abstract: Out-of-time-order correlators in random unitary circuits show a butterfly velocity set by the gate set. We connect operator growth to the entanglement velocity and to black hole scrambling bounds.

title: Distillation of magic states with fewer qubits
abstract: We present a magic-state distillation protocol that reduces the qubit overhead of the fifteen-to-one scheme by reusing ancillas. The protocol keeps the cubic error suppression.

title: Entanglement entropy as a probe of quantum phase transitions
abstract: Ground-state entanglement entropy of the transverse-field Ising model peaks at the critical point. We use this signal to locate transitions in models without known order parameters.

title: The fate of dwarf galaxies falling into galaxy clusters
abstract: Using hydrodynamic simulations we follow dwarf galaxies as they fall into massive clusters. Ram pressure removes their gas within one orbit, and tidal stripping turns many of them into ultra-diffuse galaxies.

title: Ultra-diffuse galaxies in a Perseus-like cluster environment
abstract: We identify ultra-diffuse galaxies in deep mock imaging of a simulated Perseus-like cluster. Their abundance scales with cluster mass, and most formed as normal dwarfs before entering the cluster.

title: Dark matter cores in low-mass galaxies
abstract: Repeated supernova feedback flattens the central dark matter density of low-mass galaxies. We quantify core sizes as a function of stellar mass and compare them with observed rotation curves.

title: Star formation quenching in satellite galaxies
abstract: Satellite galaxies in groups stop forming stars later than those in clusters. We measure quenching timescales from simulated orbits and find a delay of two to four billion years.

title: Tidal streams as tracers of the Milky Way halo
abstract: Stellar streams from disrupted dwarf galaxies trace the gravitational potential of the Galactic halo. We fit stream models to mock data and recover the flattening of the halo.

title: Gas stripping of dwarf galaxies by ram pressure
abstract: We run wind-tunnel simulations of dwarf galaxies moving through hot cluster gas. Stripping is fastest for edge-on orientations and leaves trailing tails of cold gas.

title: Globular cluster systems of ultra-diffuse galaxies
abstract: Rich globular cluster systems in some ultra-diffuse galaxies imply massive dark matter halos. We model cluster survival and show that tidal heating thins these systems over time.

title: Galaxy clusters as laboratories for dark matter self-interaction
abstract: Offsets between galaxies and dark matter in merging clusters constrain the self-interaction cross section. We combine twelve simulated mergers and derive an upper bound.

title: Morphological transformation of dwarfs in groups
abstract: Harassment by repeated encounters turns disky dwarf galaxies into spheroidal ones in galaxy groups. We follow morphology indicators along orbits in a cosmological simulation.

title: Measuring cluster masses with weak gravitational lensing
abstract: We calibrate weak-lensing mass estimates of galaxy clusters against simulations and quantify the bias from projected structures along the line of sight.

title: Message passing neural networks for molecular property prediction
abstract: We train message passing networks on quantum chemistry benchmarks. Edge features and a learned readout improve accuracy on dipole moments and atomization energies.

title: Over-smoothing in deep graph convolutional networks
abstract: Stacking graph convolution layers drives node representations toward a common vector. We analyse the rate of over-smoothing and show that residual connections slow it.

title: Graph attention for link prediction in knowledge graphs
abstract: We combine graph attention with relation-specific transforms for link prediction. On standard knowledge graph benchmarks the model improves mean reciprocal rank over embedding baselines.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation over knowledge graphs
abstract: Language models answer factual questions more accurately when given subgraphs retrieved around the entities in a question. We compare vector, graph and hybrid retrieval for grounding.

title: Scalable sampling for training graph neural networks
abstract: Neighbour sampling with importance weights reduces the memory cost of training on large graphs. We prove an unbiasedness result and train on graphs with a billion edges.

title: Expressive power of graph neural networks and the Weisfeiler-Lehman test
abstract: Message passing networks are at most as powerful as the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman test. We add random node identifiers and show that they separate graphs the test cannot.

title: Contrastive pretraining for graph representations
abstract: Augmenting graphs by edge dropping and feature masking gives views for contrastive learning. Pretrained encoders transfer to molecular and social network tasks with few labels.

title: Text-to-query generation with large language models
abstract: Large language models translate questions into database queries from few examples. We study errors in generated graph queries and show that schema hints and execution feedback reduce them.

title: Temporal graph networks for event forecasting
abstract: Memory modules let graph networks update node states as timestamped events arrive. We forecast interactions in communication networks and outperform static baselines.

title: Uncertainty estimation for graph neural network predictions
abstract: We compare ensembles, dropout and evidential methods for uncertainty in node classification. Ensembles are the best calibrated under distribution shift.

title: Cost-based optimization of graph pattern queries
abstract: We extend a relational optimizer with cardinality estimates for graph patterns. Join orders chosen with these estimates cut the runtime of path queries by an order of magnitude.

title: Property graphs on relational storage
abstract: Storing vertices and edges as tables with JSON properties lets a relational engine serve graph queries. We evaluate indexing strategies for property lookups and edge traversals.

title: Approximate nearest neighbour search inside a database engine
abstract: We integrate a graph-based approximate nearest neighbour index into a relational engine. Filtered searches combine the index with predicates on other columns without losing recall.

title: Workload-aware indexing for JSON documents
abstract: We recommend expression indexes over JSON paths from a query log. The recommender balances lookup speed against write amplification.

title: Hybrid search combining full-text and vector ranking
abstract: Reciprocal rank fusion merges keyword and embedding rankings without calibrating their scores. We evaluate fusion weights on news retrieval and find that the keyword weight matters most for short queries.

title: Transactional semantics for graph updates
abstract: We define isolation levels for graph mutations that touch many vertices. Snapshot isolation prevents lost updates to edge sets with modest overhead.

title: Benchmarking graph databases on social network workloads
abstract: We run interactive and analytical social network queries on several graph engines. The results depend more on index design than on the storage model.

title: Recursive queries for variable-length paths
abstract: Variable-length path patterns compile to recursive common table expressions. We bound the recursion depth and push filters into the recursion to keep traversals small.

title: Privilege separation for model-generated database queries
abstract: Queries written by language models should run under a role with only the privileges they need. We describe read-only roles, row limits and statement timeouts for graph and relational stores.

title: Change data capture for knowledge graph maintenance
abstract: Streaming row changes from operational databases keeps a knowledge graph current. We merge changes by key and measure lag under bursty update loads.
